# RESULT: Qriptal volume-anomaly candle as a filter and a veto on the lc-levels-hold level layer, BTCUSDT 1m, DEV only (generated by `run_filter.py run`)

**H1 filter: FAIL (filter lifts). H2 veto: FAIL (no veto effect).** Study word = FAIL (PASS if either primary passes; FAIL only if both fail; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE). DEV only (bars before 2024-07-01, decisions 2022-04-01..2024-06-30); VALIDATION and HOLDOUT were not read. Rules frozen in PRE_REG.md (committed before this file); one run; nothing adopted.

## Answer in numbers (fee-net R per trade, taker both legs 0.14 % round trip, 1R:1R bracket)

- The layer alone (all 5976 first-touch fades of the 8 KEEP families): net **-0.412 R** per trade at rr 1 (gross -0.062, cost 0.350), **-0.427 R** at rr 2.
- WITH a volume-anomaly small-body candle at the level (IMB, n 3271): net **-0.366 R** (SE 0.022, t -16.37); WITHOUT (n 2705): **-0.467 R**. Difference +0.101 R (SE 0.031, t +3.27, Holm p 0.017); shape-only control (n 1771): -0.454 R.
- Large-body veto: trades with a high-volume LARGE-body candle at the level (n 2702) net **-0.407 R** vs -0.416 R for the rest; difference +0.009 R (SE 0.033, t +0.27, Holm p 1.000). Removing them changes the layer from -0.412 to -0.416 R.
- Flag coverage: SMALL k2 on 54.7 % of trades, LARGE k2 on 45.2 %, CTRL-only on 29.6 %.

## Reading (written after the run; the tables above are untouched script output)

- **The imbalance condition helps, and not nearly enough.** Trades with a closed small-body volume-anomaly candle whose midpoint sits at the level lose
  0.366 R net per trade, trades without lose 0.467 R: a lift of +0.101 R (SE 0.031, Holm p 0.017, same sign in both halves: +0.092 in H1, +0.110 in H2).
  The shape-only control (same candle shape, normal volume) does no better than "no flag" (-0.454 vs -0.467 R), so the volume spike, not the candle shape, carries the lift.
  The stricter flag helps more: k = 3 (33 % of touches) lifts +0.136 R (t +4.09, unadjusted) and is the best flag cell at -0.321 R; the 1d-only flag (n 125) is -0.324 R (t -2.9).
  The pre-registered PASS needed the filtered layer to be above zero; the best flag cell is still 0.32 R below it.
- **Why: the layer has no gross edge to filter.** The 1R:1R fade of these levels earns -0.062 R gross (target 46.2 %, stop 52.6 %, time exit 1.2 %) before the 0.350 R cost
  (width 0.40 % of price at the median, cost 0.14 %). The imbalance subset is -0.017 R gross, k = 3 is +0.029 R: a filter that adds 0.10 R to a -0.06 R gross layer leaves it far under the 0.35 R fee.
  Maker entry (a readout, never a rescue) improves every cell by 0.125 R and the IMB cell is still -0.242 R. Two-R targets do not change this (-0.393 R for IMB, -0.427 R for all).
  Only two of the eight families have a positive gross (prior_day_poc +0.072, naked_poc +0.101); every family is negative net (best naked_poc -0.249 R, n 149).
- **The veto does not work on this layer.** Trades with a high-volume large-body candle at the level net -0.407 R against -0.416 R for the rest (+0.009 R, t +0.27, Holm p 1.0; k = 3: +0.006 R; rr 2: +0.024 R).
  B171's finding (fading a high-volume large-body candle at a 20-bar extreme loses 0.10-0.42 R gross) is about fading that candle; as a veto on level fades it adds nothing. Not supported, not killed beyond this layer.
- **Power is not the issue.** The day-clustered MDE of Delta1 is 0.086 R and of Delta2 0.092 R, both under the 0.15 R bar, so both FAILs stand (they are not downgraded to INCONCLUSIVE).
- **The sub-label "filter lifts"** follows PRE_REG section 4 literally: (c) and (d) hold, (b) fails. Condition (e) (above the shape-only control) also held (-0.366 vs -0.454 R). The only failed condition is the one that matters for money: (b), IMB mean net R > 0.

## Caveats the reader needs

- The flag is common (SMALL k2 on 54.7 % of touches, 45 % of touches via a 1h candle alone), because a 7-day window of 1h candles puts many midpoints within 0.25 % of a level. Part of the contrast is therefore "busy price area vs quiet" rather than Qriptal's single marked imbalance; the k = 3 and 4h/12h/1d rows are closer to his use and show the same sign.
  Volume anomalies cluster in active periods; the halves and the shape-only control do not remove that confound. No regime control was pre-registered.
- Touch fill at the level is the lc assumption and the optimistic one; stops are filled stop-first. Cost uses 0.14 % round trip; at a 0.40 % width that is 0.35 R, so the result is about the layer's width as much as the filter.
- PRE_REG section 6 guessed about 20 touches per day; the count was 7.3 per day (5,976 on 818 days: levels per day are fewer after the KEEP filter and the price dedup, and only the first touch counts). No gate depended on that guess.
- Overlapping trades of one day are separate observations; every SE and t is day-clustered (818 days). Day-clustering treats days as independent, and 2022-2024 BTC regimes were not.
- The third part of his rule (a wick reaction before entry) is NOT tested: here the entry is at the touch and the reaction is the outcome. A wick-confirmation entry, imbalance mid/open as the level source, other exchanges (he reads Coinbase and Bybit separately) and his undisclosed threshold remain untested.

## Defects found while building this (reported, no lc file edited)

1. LC2 `levels_confluence_2026-10-14/event_table.py:134` sets `side = 1 if float(b['c']) >= px else -1` with b = the touch bar, so the trade direction reads the CLOSE of the bar in which the entry happens (look-ahead inside the 1m bar). LC1's `levels_hold.py:_touch_side` and `outcome()` do the same, and credit a favourable move inside the touch bar. This study uses the previous bar's close for the side and gives the touch bar no target credit; the layer's hit rate here (46 % target, 53 % stop) is therefore not comparable with LC1's HOLD rates (54-69 %).
2. The lc study's DEV (2024-12..2025-03, `levels_hold.md`) lies inside the standard VALIDATION window (2024-07-01..2025-06-30), so `event_table.csv` carries VALIDATION outcomes (MFE/MAE). It was not read here. The KEEP list is used as a given; it was not tuned on the 2022-04..2024-06 bars.

## Kill scope

FAIL means stop: the Qriptal volume-anomaly candle (midpoint of a closed 1h/4h/12h/1d candle within 0.25 % of the level, k 2 or 3, small body) as a FILTER on first-touch fades of the lc-levels-hold KEEP levels with a 1R or 2R bracket at the LC1 width, and the large-body candle as a VETO on the same trades, under 0.14 % round-trip cost. It says nothing about other level sources, a wick-confirmation entry, wider stops or higher-RR exits that dilute the fee, or imbalance candles used as the level itself.
Next step if the operator wants this idea tested further: a new PRE_REG whose fee share is under 0.10 R (stop width at least 1.4 % of price, i.e. 4h-1d structure), because the filter's +0.10..+0.14 R is real on DEV but smaller than the fee at the 0.40 % width.

## DECISION (OURS) lines

- D1: standard DEV (bars before 2024-07-01, decisions from 2022-04-01) and rebuilt touches instead of the lc event table, which is VALIDATION data under the standard split.
- D2: "at the level" = candle midpoint within 0.25 % (his mid/open usage, `imb.level_match` "mid"), chosen in PRE_REG before any count; the range-hold alternative would flag about 80 % of touches by a hand estimate and was not run.
- D3: the count step ran after the PRE_REG commit and before the outcome run; no definition was changed after seeing counts (shares 54.7 % / 45.2 %, not degenerate).
- D4: stratification by family uses the first family of a joined price (prior_day_poc before naked_poc).
- D5: Holm m = 16 uses `verdicts.py count --split DEV` = 14 on 2026-10-16 plus the two primaries.
